chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out to his companions and said: 'What has gathered you?' They replied: 'We have gathered to mention our Lord and to ponder upon His Greatness.' He said: 'You will not attain [the true reality of] pondering upon His Greatness.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the companions' reflection on God's greatness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, the Prophet (SAW) cautions his companions that mere intellectual reflection (*tafakkur*) on God’s attributes is insufficient to comprehend His true essence, a concept central to the Shia doctrine of *Tajsim* (anthropomorphism) and the limits of human reason. This highlights the necessity of combining rational contemplation with divine revelation and spiritual insight to avoid reducing the Infinite to finite human categories. The narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transcendence (*Tanzih*) of Allah, where His greatness ultimately exceeds full human conceptualization.
